env:exterior.text: The FRESHWAY sign is cut off at both edges. Pull the camera back ~4 m (or an 18 mm lens) so the store name reads: it's the only establishing text in the episode.
Beyond the two lamps the lot is black. Add 2–3 more sodium lamps along the storefront so the horde stands in pools of orange light in every exterior shot.

env:inside_glass.text: The green exit-sign glow dominates the top of the frame. Halve its light so the glass and the parking lot read first.

env:front_aisle.text: Too clean for a store you've been trapped in for 7 hours. Scatter debris near the front aisle: fallen cans, an overturned cart, a dropped basket.
Add one fixture that flickers for the whole episode (deterministic flicker), so the space never feels completely still.

env:toy_aisle.text: The story's key location is nearly black until the toys light up. Make the toy-aisle fixture part of the set (a dim, failing light) instead of an episode event, so every angle on aisle 6 reads.

env:overview.text: Unreadable at this exposure (4/255) and it repeats the other angles. Replace with a high wide from above the checkouts looking down the aisles toward the glow of aisle 6.

cast:you.text: You stand up fully to reach the toy ('interact'). Staying low (crouch then reach) fits 'every step is a gunshot'. I'd add a crouched-reach action.
'You take off your shoes' has no visual payoff: the mannequin has no shoes. Either give 'you' sneakers that come off in the shoes shot, or rewrite n4 (e.g. 'So you hold your breath.').

cast:zombie.text: Grey-green bodies vanish in the dark lot. Give zombies a faint sickly-yellow tint and dim glowing eyes so their silhouettes read at night.
Between cues the horde is static. Let the back rows shuffle (zombie_walk in place / slow drift) so the crowd feels alive.

cast:zombie_f.text: Same as zombie: faint tint + dim eyes for readability at night.

voice:script.text: 'Seven hours' appears 3 times. A sharper last line: 'You'd survive seven hours. The toys? They were just getting started.'
Hook: in n1 the narrator repeats 'let's play'. Let the toy's own voice say it again there instead (scarier, and it ties the sound to the threat).

voice:n5a.text: This is the draft voice (lite model) and it drags here. Re-review after the full-model take, when the free quota resets.

voice:n8.text: Slow is right for the quiet beat, but trim the pause between the two sentences by ~0.4 s.

voice:toy3.text: Make the final chorus more wrong: end each copy with a dying-battery pitch drop, so it isn't just a louder repeat of the first line.

shot:toy_wakes.text: Strongest possible hook: show zombie silhouettes at the glass, out of focus, far behind the toy in frame 1, so the threat is on screen in the first second.

shot:horde_turns.text: The turn lands ~0.9 s into the shot. Put it right on the cut for impact, and add a slow push toward the glass (5.9 s is long for a static frame).

shot:glass_wall.text: Your back fills a third of the frame and the horde reads small. Lower the camera and use a 50 mm lens so the zombies at the glass loom behind you.

shot:long_aisle.text: The toy looks close here, against 'forty meters away'. An 18 mm lens from floor level would exaggerate the distance.

shot:shoes.text: Floor-level close-up on your feet as you start to move (ties to the shoes line; depends on the cast:you shoes decision).

shot:toy_again.text: Lengthen the flicker (0.6 → 1.2 s) and land a glass bang exactly on the cut.

shot:creak.text: Too dark to read. Go closer: one zombie hand flat on the glass, backlit by a parking lamp, the glass flexing.

shot:reach.text: Works. Tighten to an over-the-shoulder on 'pull the batteries' so the eyes going dark are the focus.

shot:silence.text: The wide is unreadable. Try a high angle over the checkouts: the whole store still, the frozen horde silhouetted against the lamps.

shot:seven_hours.text: 8.8 s on one static frame. Slow push-in on your face, then cut to an insert of the dead toy in your hand on 'perfect silence'.

shot:all_toys.text: The payoff is only 2.4 s. Hold for 3.5 s and add a short camera shake on the sting.

shot:ending.text: Cut to black right on 'plans.' and let the toy chorus echo over the black, instead of holding the shelf.
